question_defect: The question says "average velocity of a particles of the gas". Velocity is a vector and its average over the molecules of a gas at rest is zero; the quantity meant is the average (or rms) SPEED. "a particles" is also a typographical slip for "the particles". Neither changes which option fits.
notes: My own solve: speed varies as sqrt(T), so a factor 4 in speed is a factor 16 in absolute temperature. T_final = 300 x 16 = 4800 K = 4800 - 273 = 4527 °C, option 2. Verified in python. Both mistake entries check out numerically: subtracting 300 instead of 273 gives 4500 °C (option 1), and multiplying T by 4 instead of 16 gives 1200 K = 927 °C. Using 273.15 instead of 273 gives 4526.85 °C, which still rounds to option 2, so the choice of 273 is not a finding.
